discovery: Moiré flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states (twistronics)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly Tel Aviv University)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and correlated electrons
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the moire superlattice of two graphene layers produces nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero's group (Nature 2018) realized this with a simple, bold fabrication trick, tear-and-stack assembly of van der Waals layers, and discovered correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in a pure-carbon system whose carrier density is tuned by a gate. This created an entirely new experimental platform: the twist angle became a control knob for electronic structure. Hundreds of laboratories worldwide have since built on it, uncovering orbital ferromagnetism, the quantized anomalous Hall effect, fractional Chern insulators and correlated phases in moire transition-metal dichalcogenides. Few recent discoveries have opened so broad and reproducible a field for strongly correlated and topological physics.
